page: Google Cloud Platform e2-medium is a shared-core virtual machine instance belonging to the e2 server family. It is configured with 2 vCPUs mapped to a single shared physical core of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz, supporting hyper-threading with two threads per core. The instance includes 4.0 GB of x86_64 system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not feature any bundled local storage or dedicated GPU hardware accelerators, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate a distinct asymmetry between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance achieves a strong single-core CPU performance score of 2642.19 in stress-ng tests, placing it in the top 25 percent. However, its multi-core CPU performance is weak at 2642.78, falling into the bottom 25 percent. Memory bandwidth is highly constrained, with read-only large block speeds at 6.36 GB/sec and write speeds at 4.83 GB/sec, both ranking in the bottom 10 percent. Similarly, database operations and Redis SET performance are limited, with Redis handling 0.82 million operations per second.

Due to its shared-core architecture and low memory bandwidth, the e2-medium is designed as a budget-friendly option for workloads with low resource density. It is not suitable for memory-intensive databases, large-scale LLM inference, or high-throughput web serving. Instead, it is best utilized for lightweight background tasks, small-scale static web serving, basic single-threaded scripting, or development and testing environments where continuous high CPU utilization is not required.
